pr_title: Predictable generation of import library on Windows.
pr_comment:

I also wonder why `def_parser` is named so, given that it parses object files and generates `def`.

@excitoon Thanks for this contribution! I named it as `def_parser` exactly because it generates DEF file. Sorry if it's a bit confusing, I was just finding it a bit difficult to keep the name short and precise.

@meteorcloudy I'm done with changes. The only thing I don't get is why in `testGetDefFileOfSharedLibraryFromCcBinary` even without `windows_exports_all_symbols` we've checked that all symbols are in DEF file. After my change, in that case DEF file has no symbols.

I've just looked into `def_parser` and found that it does actually parse DEF files (I guess for transitive gathering of symbols?), but currently this mechanism is not used because only object files are being passed through it:
https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/blame/master/src/main/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/rules/cpp/CppHelper.java#L806

> The only thing I don't get is why in testGetDefFileOfSharedLibraryFromCcBinary even without windows_exports_all_symbols we've checked that all symbols are in DEF file.

Previously, the DEF file is always generated by parsing the object files, you can get the file by `def_file` output group. But without `windows_exports_all_symbols` feature it won't be passed to the linker. 

This behavior is actually used at 
https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/blob/38fd4259e1febcb59ea51dea1d2eed2c43ed80e3/tensorflow/BUILD#L586-L590

Do you think you can keep the original behavior?

> I've just looked into `def_parser` and found that it does actually parse DEF files (I guess for transitive gathering of symbols?), but currently this mechanism is not used because only object files are being passed through it:
> https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/blame/master/src/main/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/rules/cpp/CppHelper.java#L806

That's correct.

@meteorcloudy Is it possible that they just add `windows_export_all_symbols` feature for these targets? I can keep original behavior if I add second DEF file which would only exist if `windows_export_all_symbols` is disabled. But I don't see it as a clean solution.
@excitoon OK, if adding `windows_export_all_symbols` gives the DEF file containing parsed symbols, I'm fine with that.
I guess I shall make it as an incompatible change fix.

@excitoon Incompatible change sounds good, but this feature is only being used for TensorFlow on Windows, I would be surprised if anyone else is using it. I can easily send a change to add the `windows_export_all_symbols` feature. So I'm also ok with not going through the incompatible flags process.
@meteorcloudy I'm perfectly fine with not going through this process. Not blocking it anymore.
@excitoon this PR seems to be very useful for solving https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/issues/4561, do you have time to get it merged?
https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/pull/9976 is a replacement of this PR. This one can be closed.

review_comment: Why do we need this condition here? This could be the cause of the `NullPointerException`

I guess the cause of `NullPointerException` here is using generated DEF file in `def_parser`. That makes `def_parser` to depend on `def_parser`. I shall write independent action which would output `LIBRARY nnn` line to DEF file.

https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/blob/1f684e1b87cd8881a0a4b33e86ba66743e32d674/src/main/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/bazel/rules/cpp/BazelCppRuleClasses.java#L271 explains why Bazel didn't catch the cycle dependency issue. We're actually explicitly not adding def_parser as a dependency of itself.
